svg.title: DRAFT: Courier return ticket, reconcile an air-gapped delivery without a live connection
svg.desc: Illustrative, non-interactive concept. A sending station exported one signed bundle for the isolated foundry site. The station's export half is known, but the site's return half is absent: import, rollout and device execution are unknown. A physical boundary separates these halves. The operator chooses to request a return ticket rather than send a replacement blindly. The ticket would contain signed, privacy-minimized import evidence tied to the exact bundle, not employee or device inventory. Export success is not import success; verified import does not start a rollout, and feed freshness remains anchored to acquisition time. A new signed return artifact and console exchange records require backend design.

Missing ticket is not a failed import.

Proposed authenticated artifact, not a live status
Physical transfer
Decision: close the information gap before replacing the delivery
Ask the site operator for a ticket bound to this exact bundle and its verified import result.
Expiry or rejection must be reported as such. A copied filename is not proof of identity.
What bringing back a ticket would do
Verify the site's claim and reconcile this exchange. Reject untrusted or replayed return artifacts.
No rollout starts. No new device health is inferred. Import proposals remain paused until authorized.
Proposed contents: bundle binding, site identity, observed import result and time; no device/user inventory.
Prepare return-ticket instructions
Review a replacement delivery instead
PROPOSED: signed return artifact + exchange record. Existing bundle verification does not supply this UI.
